task_objective: Downgrade prose-shaped values matched by the three quoted secret rules, expose only non-identifying value-shape evidence, and restore DeckTools after a clean re-audit.

setup.remote_dev_pull: Attempted git pull --ff-only origin dev; origin has no dev ref, so the clean local dev tip c2b5ee4 was used as the required base.
setup.plan_history: The plan was already committed as the dev tip, so feat/secret-value-precision inherited the required plan-first commit instead of creating a duplicate empty commit.
setup.tooling: The repository has no run.sh. XDG_CACHE_HOME was isolated under /tmp because the sandboxed global uv cache was read-only. The live re-audit reused Trivy 0.73.0 and ClamAV 1.4.5 with packaged signature databases staged under /tmp; no host packages were installed.

implementation.credential_shape: generic_api_key, bearer_token and cloudflare_token now downgrade a matched value containing any Unicode whitespace to PASS_WITH_WARNINGS while retaining the finding. Existing fixture and placeholder downgrades remain unchanged.
implementation.natural_language_scope: The whitespace rule handles every required prose example. A vowel-proportion heuristic was deliberately not added because it would also downgrade plausible letter-only credentials; the plan explicitly permits shipping the high-confidence whitespace rule alone when the broader heuristic is unreliable.
implementation.pattern_scope: github_token, aws_key, private_key_header and password_literal classification behavior was not changed. The existing _PLACEHOLDER_SECRET_PATTERNS membership remains exactly biconditional with patterns that define a named value group.
implementation.evidence: Every secret finding now reports value_length, contains_whitespace and entirely_alphabetic alongside the existing match position and redaction marker. Alphabetic means every non-whitespace character is alphabetic, matching the review distinction between spaced prose and mixed credentials. Values, substrings and hashes are never included.

decktools_re_audit.secret_finding: DeckTools/dist/index.js:523 remains visible as SECRET_GENERIC_API_KEY / PASS_WITH_WARNINGS with value_length=16, contains_whitespace=yes and entirely_alphabetic=yes.
decktools_re_audit.disposition: Added back. The sole prior BLOCK was the Portuguese UI label false positive. The surviving subprocess, loader-environment, mount, SteamOS read-only, sudo, root and Steam-auth findings are expected manual-review or warning signals for a system-tools plugin, and no blocking finding remains.
decktools_re_audit.durable_verdict: security-verdicts.json records MANUAL_REVIEW for v0.6.0@437908781 with no blocking rule IDs.

not_verified: This change does not improve recall. A real credential containing whitespace is now downgraded, which is the plan's accepted tradeoff against BLOCK-severity prose false positives.
No vowel-proportion natural-language heuristic was added because it could downgrade plausible letter-only credentials.
Only DeckTools was re-audited. Other stored reports will naturally miss cache lookups when audit_plugins.py changes the audit context hash.
